assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral-constrained borrowing, with its amplification and propagation of shocks, is a foundational mechanism in macro-finance. It is central to how financial frictions are modelled and to the post-2008 policy debate. The framework has had very broad influence on macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) is the clear originating contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the financial accelerator and its empirical side, but that strand overlaps with work already recognised in 2022. A two-person award is the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of citation, extension and use in policy models. There is ample time to judge its lasting value.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to include Gertler or Gilchrist for the financial-accelerator strand
Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises could reduce the perceived novelty
Direct empirical validation of the mechanism is more mixed than the theory's influence suggests

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices and unobserved heterogeneity changed empirical industrial organisation. The methods are used in merger review, antitrust, trade, health and environmental economics. They are widely taken up well outside the original field.
assessment.attribution: The BLP framework (Berry 1994; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes 1995) is a clear core. Pakes also contributed the dynamic industry framework and later estimation work. The longlist credits others (Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard, Levin) whose contributions are real but separate, so the three-name limit forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of intensive use in academia and regulatory practice. The contribution has stood up well.
uncertainties: Bresnahan's and Reiss's earlier contributions to empirical IO might be thought to deserve credit
Reasonable disagreement on whether this is a methods prize or a prize for substantive discovery
Identification and the sensitivity of results to functional form remain debated

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Formal models of present bias, self-control problems and reference dependence brought psychologically realistic preferences into mainstream economics. They have applications in savings, health, contract design and policy. The influence is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Rabin is central to both the present-bias and reference-dependence strands. Laibson is the leading figure on quasi-hyperbolic discounting and its life-cycle implications. Loewenstein contributed psychologically grounded concepts and evidence. Koszegi and O'Donoghue are also strong, so the three-name cap makes the attribution contestable. Prior prizes to Kahneman and Thaler cover part of the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Core papers date from the 1990s and 2000s, with decades of replication and application. Timing is not an obstacle.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 and 2017 prizes could lower the marginal case
Replicability of some behavioural findings is debated
Loewenstein's contribution is more conceptual and experimental than formal, which may weaken the grouping

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Linking population-scale administrative records to measure mobility, neighbourhood effects and the long-run returns to policies changed what can be measured empirically. It reshaped public and labour economics and informs policy design in many countries.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the leading figure and a driving force in the data work. Hendren and Friedman are co-authors on key contributions (neighbourhood effects, the marginal value of public funds, teacher value-added). Katz's work on Moving to Opportunity is important but only part of the broader mobility literature. The collective, team-based nature of the research makes crediting difficult.
assessment.maturity: The most influential work is from roughly 2011 to 2022. Its impact is substantial and growing, but the long-run durability of some findings is not yet fully tested.
uncertainties: The work is relatively recent compared with the other top-ranked candidates
Causal interpretation of place-based estimates and replication of the quasi-experimental results are still being argued
Chetty also appears in the public economics candidate, so credit across the two candidates is not independent

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave a tractable, strategic foundation for bargaining. Its extension to decentralised markets links bargaining to search and trade. It is a pillar of modern game theory and has been applied in labour, industrial organisation and monetary models.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the clear originating contribution. Rubinstein and Wolinsky (1985) extend it to markets. Binmore's related work developed and interpreted the model, but the central credit is with Rubinstein, and Wolinsky is the natural second name.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of consolidation. Very mature, with a risk that its time as a prize-winning topic has passed.
uncertainties: Existing prizes to game theorists and mechanism designers might make the committee reluctant to add another theory prize
Empirical and policy impact is indirect compared with applied candidates
Whether Binmore's contribution warrants a place

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantifying how resource misallocation across firms lowers aggregate productivity gave a concrete account of cross-country income differences. It redirected development and growth research toward micro-level productivity measurement and policy distortions. The influence is large.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the key paper. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) developed a closely related argument, but Rogerson is not credited on the longlist. Restuccia is credited and his role in the broader programme is significant. A two-person award is the most defensible.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years of heavy use. It is established, though the empirical interpretation continues to evolve.
uncertainties: Measured misallocation may partly reflect measurement error and unobserved heterogeneity
Rogerson's absence from the credited names complicates attribution
Whether the contribution is better viewed as a measurement framework or a theory of development

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory explained why only some firms export and why gains from trade come through reallocation. It changed trade empirics and policy analysis after the 'new trade theory'. Krugman's earlier prize covers a related but distinct body of work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central paper. Helpman contributed to the wider heterogeneity and trade framework, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exports versus foreign direct investment. Redding's work is substantial, especially on quantitative applications. The credit is concentrated but multi-person.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of consolidation, with the framework now standard in graduate teaching and applied work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the quantitative trade candidate (B001) and the trade-politics candidate (B043) complicates attribution
Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum also contributed to the early firm-level evidence and are not credited here
Quantitative welfare implications are debated

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Empirical work on the labour-market effects of import competition and on task-based technological change reshaped understanding of inequality, local labour markets and the distributional costs of trade. It also shaped public and policy debate across many countries.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the three core authors of the 'China shock' papers, so attribution there is clean. Autor also has foundational task-based work with Levy and Murnane, and with Katz. Katz is credited but his contribution is the broader skill-biased change literature.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from 2013 onward, with significant follow-up work. Impact is substantial but still being assessed for robustness and persistence.
uncertainties: Debate about identification and the size of the effects
Relatively recent, so lasting impact is less proven
The task-based and trade-shock strands may be considered separate contributions
